$comment: Mission 1.70 §31 to §35. Architecture only. Nothing was fetched, crawled or built, and nothing is authorised here.
why_it_is_considered: The population decision established that an externally frozen population with distinguishable missingness cannot be obtained from either archive. An operator-run fetcher supplies both properties by construction. It is considered because of that, not because building something is attractive.

what_it_would_solve: population directability, which neither archive offers
attempt-level coverage, which neither archive documents
missingness legibility, which is what strategy P5 needs
request-contract control, which the compatibility table shows is otherwise unestablished on eleven fields

governance_feasibility.$comment: §33. This mission does NOT authorise it.
governance_feasibility.the_mechanism_is_not_novel: This repository already operates reviewed collectors that make HTTP requests to third parties under an authorization context. A bounded, identified, rate-limited request for a public page is not a new kind of act for it.
governance_feasibility.what_is_novel_and_why_a_review_is_needed: Every source in the registry is a named publisher, and a fixed-corpus fetcher measures many third-party sites none of which is a registered source. The source-governance model has no shape for 'a corpus of arbitrary public sites', and inventing one in passing is the change-control shape docs/CLAUDE.md refuses.
conditions_a_future_review_would_have_to: ordinary HTTP or HTTPS with no authentication
conservative rate limits and per-domain throttling
an explicit, frozen robots and policy handling rule
no bypass, no circumvention, no anti-bot evasion
no vulnerability probing and no destructive requests
GET or HEAD only, if later approved
explicit timeouts and no crawling expansion beyond the corpus

questions_a_later_mission_must_answer: independent from WHICH external apparatus, named
whether measurement production is genuinely separate
whether corpus or predicate selection could have been influenced by seeing external values
whether run ordering can prevent contamination
whether external values can remain unseen until the operator run is sealed
whether two runs sharing DNS and Internet state remain distinct apparatus observations
safeguards_it_would_require: an ordering rule where ordering is load-bearing

fallback_not_forced_solution.statement: If the two archives had qualified directly, no operator fetcher would be proposed. They did not, and only on population. So this is the fallback the mission was told to consider in exactly that case.
fallback_not_forced_solution.and_it_gets_no_exemption: One operator fetcher plus one archive must still satisfy the same-proposition requirement. Being ours does not relax it, and the archive's coverage semantics would still have to be legible for the pair to share a population.
fallback_not_forced_solution.the_honest_residual: An operator fetcher fixes OUR side of the population problem. It does not fix the archive's, so a pair would still need one archive whose attempt-level coverage is documented. That is the question the next mission inherits.
